advances:
This gives an explicit universal lower bound for the cap-shape modulus
\(\Delta_Q\) throughout the whole retained fixed-ratio \(D\)-interval.  It
also converts the boxed ledger inequality in accepted fact
`6e4bb19f9157027f` into one explicit lower bound on the full-body coverage
slack \(\Xi\).  Thus the remaining gap is sharply localized: cap geometry
already contributes the displayed positive modulus, and any unresolved
realization must violate the displayed \(\Xi\)-bound strictly.
author: /root/mp_r54_synthesis
proof:
We first extract an active short-gap pair from the exact \(A_2\) normal
form.  Write
\[
s_i=1-L_i=a_{i,i^-}+a_{i,i^+}.
\]
The coordinate central-cell formula in accepted fact
`c49613ac26c0c4a8` is
\[
D
=1-(1-\rho_{12})a_{12}a_{21}
  -(1-\rho_{23})a_{23}a_{32}
  -(1-\rho_{31})a_{31}a_{13}.
\]
Since \(0\le\rho_{ij}\le1\),
\[
F:=a_{12}a_{21}+a_{23}a_{32}+a_{31}a_{13}
\ge1-D.
\tag{11}
\]

We claim that some active cyclic pair \((i,j)\), meaning
\(a_{ij}a_{ji}>0\), satisfies
\[
s_is_j\ge F.
\tag{12}
\]
For positive \(s_i\), write
\[
a_{12}=s_1\alpha,\quad a_{13}=s_1(1-\alpha),
\]
\[
a_{21}=s_2\beta,\quad a_{23}=s_2(1-\beta),
\]
\[
a_{31}=s_3\gamma,\quad a_{32}=s_3(1-\gamma),
\qquad 0\le\alpha,\beta,\gamma\le1.
\]
If \(H\) is the largest \(s_is_j\) among active pairs, then
\[
\begin{aligned}
F
&=s_1s_2\alpha\beta
 +s_2s_3(1-\beta)(1-\gamma)
 +s_3s_1\gamma(1-\alpha)\\
&\le
H\bigl(
\alpha\beta+(1-\beta)(1-\gamma)
+\gamma(1-\alpha)
\bigr)
\le H.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
The last bracket is at most \(1\), because its complement is
\[
\alpha\gamma+\beta(1-\alpha-\gamma),
\]
which is nonnegative when \(\alpha+\gamma\le1\), while for
\(\alpha+\gamma\ge1\) its minimum over \(0\le\beta\le1\) is
\((1-\alpha)(1-\gamma)\ge0\).  A term belonging to an inactive pair is
zero, so it does not require its coefficient to be bounded by \(H\).
Zero \(s_i\) follow by deleting their identically zero incident terms.
Since (11) is positive, at least one pair is active.  This proves (12).

Choose such an active pair and relabel it as \((1,2)\).  Equations
(11)--(12) give
\[
(1-L_1)(1-L_2)=s_1s_2\ge1-D.
\]
Arithmetic--geometric mean gives
\[
L_1+L_2
\le2\bigl(1-\sqrt{1-D}\bigr)=2r(D),
\]
and hence
\[
z=L_1L_2\le r(D)^2.
\tag{14}
\]
The endpoint-pair convention in `c49613ac26c0c4a8` says that activity
means \(a_{12},a_{21}>0\), so no division by a zero endpoint is used.

We next prove the pairwise mixed-area estimate (4).  In barycentric
coordinates \(e_1=(1,0),e_2=(0,1),e_3=(0,0)\), translate the two cap
triangles independently.  They have the forms
\[
\widehat C_1
=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(0,L_1),(-h_1,\alpha_0)\},
\]
\[
\widehat C_2
=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(L_2,0),(\beta_0,-h_2)\},
\tag{15}
\]
where
\[
L_1h_1=L_2h_2=t.
\tag{16}
\]
Indeed, the coordinate cap area in `c49613ac26c0c4a8` is
\[
\frac{Dx}{2q}=\frac{5D}{42}=\frac t2.
\]

Let \(A=a_{12}>0\) and \(B=a_{21}>0\).  In the untranslated normal-form
coordinates,
\[
p_{12}=(0,A),\qquad p_{21}=(B,0),
\]
\[
u_1=(-h_1,A+\alpha_0),\qquad
u_2=(B+\beta_0,-h_2).
\]
The cyclic boundary order in `c49613ac26c0c4a8` contains
\[
u_1,p_{12},z_{12},p_{21},u_2.
\]
The determinant constraint for the directed edge \(u_1p_{12}\), tested
at \(p_{21}\), is
\[
\alpha_0B-h_1A\ge0.
\]
The determinant constraint for the directed edge \(p_{21}u_2\), tested
at \(p_{12}\), is
\[
\beta_0A-h_2B\ge0.
\]
Thus
\[
\alpha_0>0,\qquad \beta_0>0,\qquad
\alpha_0\beta_0\ge h_1h_2.
\tag{17}
\]
These are closed convex-order consequences, so coincident or redundant
central labels cause no exception.

For completeness, compute the mixed area directly.  The
counterclockwise edge vectors of \(\widehat C_1\) in (15) have outward
normal vectors
\[
(L_1,0),\qquad
(\alpha_0-L_1,h_1),\qquad
(-\alpha_0,-h_1).
\]
For polygons \(K,L\), differentiating the edge-support formula for
\(|K+\varepsilon L|\) at \(\varepsilon=0\) gives
\[
2V(K,L)=\sum_{e\ {\rm edge\ of}\ K}h_L(n_e),
\tag{18}
\]
where \(n_e\) is the clockwise rotation of the directed edge vector and
therefore already has the edge length built in.  Applying (18) to (15)
gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
2V(\widehat C_1,\widehat C_2)
&=
L_1\max\{0,L_2,\beta_0\}\\
&\quad+
\max\{0,(\alpha_0-L_1)L_2,
(\alpha_0-L_1)\beta_0-h_1h_2\}\\
&\quad+
\max\{0,-\alpha_0L_2,
h_1h_2-\alpha_0\beta_0\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
To justify (18) directly, translate \(L\) arbitrarily.  Each supporting
line of an edge \(e\) of \(K\) moves outward to first order by
\(\varepsilon h_L(n_e)/|e|\), adding a strip of first-order area
\(\varepsilon h_L(n_e)\); all vertex wedges have area
\(O(\varepsilon^2)\).  Summing the strips gives the derivative in (18),
and translation does not change the sum because the directed edge
normals sum to zero.
The last maximum is \(0\) by (17).

Put
\[
u=\frac{\alpha_0}{L_1},\qquad
v=\frac{\beta_0}{L_2},\qquad
R=\frac tz.
\]
Equations (16)--(17) imply \(uv\ge R^2\).  Dropping only nonnegative
candidates from the maxima in (19) yields
\[
\frac{2V(\widehat C_1,\widehat C_2)}z
\ge
\max\{1,v\}+\max\{0,u-1\}.
\tag{20}
\]
If \(u,v\ge1\), the right side is at least
\[
u+v-1\ge2\sqrt{uv}-1\ge2R-1.
\]
If \(u<1\), then \(v>R^2\), and if \(v<1\), then \(u>R^2\).  In either
case (20) is at least \(R^2\ge2R-1\).  Therefore
\[
2V(\widehat C_1,\widehat C_2)
\ge z(2R-1)=2t-z.
\tag{21}
\]

It remains to check that \(R>1\) on the retained interval.  Since
\[
D_*<\frac17<\frac{105}{169},
\]
accepted fact `b8e22f6a4b26ea94` gives \(D<105/169\): its constant
\(c_0\) is at least \(6/7\), and substitution of \(6/7\) in its
threshold is exactly \(D_*\).  If
\(r=r(D)\), then \(D=r(2-r)\), and
\[
r^2<\frac{5D}{21}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
r<\frac5{13}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
D<\frac{105}{169}.
\tag{22}
\]
Equations (14) and (22) prove \(z<t\), so (21) proves (4).

For the other two cap pairs, planar Brunn--Minkowski, in the mixed-area
form proved in accepted fact `7bb6cb9b365924a5`, gives
\[
V(\widehat C_i,\widehat C_j)\ge\frac t2.
\]
Using (21), the coordinate Minkowski-sum area is therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\widehat C_1+\widehat C_2+\widehat C_3|
&=
3\frac t2+2\sum_{i<j}V(\widehat C_i,\widehat C_j)\\
&\ge
\frac{3t}{2}+(2t-z)+t+t
=\frac{11t}{2}-z.
\end{aligned}
\tag{23}
\]
The physical area multiplier in `c49613ac26c0c4a8` is \(2q/D\).
Thus (14) and (23) give
\[
|C_1+C_2+C_3|
\ge
\frac{2q}{D}\left(\frac{11t}{2}-z\right)
\ge
q\left(\frac{55}{21}-\frac{2r(D)^2}{D}\right),
\]
which is (5).  Rationalizing
\[
\frac{r(D)^2}{D}
=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-D}}{1+\sqrt{1-D}}
\]
proves the second expression in (1).

Equation (22) also gives
\[
G(D)-\frac{15}{7}
=\frac{2}{D}\left(t-r(D)^2\right)>0.
\tag{24}
\]
Moreover \(r(D)^2/D\) is increasing in \(D\), so \(G(D)\) is decreasing.
Since \(D<D_*\), equations (5) and (24) prove (6), using the definition
\[
\Delta_Q=\sqrt{|C_1+C_2+C_3|}-3\sqrt{x}
\]
from accepted fact `7bb6cb9b365924a5`.

The same accepted fact proves mixed-area additivity and the planar
Minkowski inequality.  Therefore
\[
\sum_i\mathcal V(P,C_i)
=\mathcal V(P,C_1+C_2+C_3)
\ge\sqrt{p|C_1+C_2+C_3|},
\]
and (5) proves (7).

Substitute (7) into the left side of the boxed ledger target in accepted
fact `6e4bb19f9157027f`.  The resulting sufficient condition is
\[
\frac32\sqrt{pqG(D)}+3\Xi
\ge
\frac{39p}{4}+w_P-\frac{1839q}{28}.
\]
Dividing by \(3\) and collecting terms gives exactly (8).  That accepted
fact proves that its boxed ledger inequality excludes \(W=0\), so every
unresolved realization must violate (8) strictly.

Finally, at the fixed ratio \(m=12q/7\).  Scaling all areas by \(1/m\)
leaves \(D\) unchanged and sends \(q\) to \(7/12\).  The strict inequality
\(Dp_{\varnothing}<7/12\) in accepted fact `4ee2807833cea34e` therefore
rescales to (2).  Dividing the strict failure of (8) by \(q\), and using
\(\Xi\ge0\) from accepted fact `6e4bb19f9157027f`, gives precisely
(9)--(10).  This proves every assertion.
statement:
Assume all the hypotheses and notation of accepted fact
`6e4bb19f9157027f`.  Thus
\[
q=q_{123}>0,\qquad
x_1=x_2=x_3=x=\frac{5q}{21},\qquad
D=\frac{q}{|\mathcal T_Q|},
\]
\[
P=\overline{P_\varnothing},\qquad p=|P|=p_\varnothing,
\qquad
C_i=\overline{Q_{N\setminus\{i\}}},
\]
and \(w_P,\Xi,\mathcal V(P,C_i)\) have the meanings fixed there.
Use the accepted \(A_2\) normal form `c49613ac26c0c4a8`, including all
eight endpoint-pair strata.  Put
\[
D_*=\frac{343}{2460+48\sqrt{51}},
\qquad
r(D)=1-\sqrt{1-D},
\qquad
t=\frac{5D}{21},
\]
and
\[
G(D)
=\frac{55}{21}-\frac{2r(D)^2}{D}
=\frac{13+97\sqrt{1-D}}
       {21\bigl(1+\sqrt{1-D}\bigr)}.
\tag{1}
\]
Accepted fact `b8e22f6a4b26ea94` gives \(0<D<D_*\), and accepted fact
`4ee2807833cea34e`, after undoing its normalization \(m=1\), gives
\[
Dp<q.
\tag{2}
\]

In the normal form there is a cyclic endpoint pair \((i,j)\) for which
\[
a_{ij}>0,\qquad a_{ji}>0,
\qquad
z:=L_iL_j\le r(D)^2<t.
\tag{3}
\]
For this pair the coordinate cap triangles satisfy the strict
pairwise mixed-area improvement
\[
2V(\widehat C_i,\widehat C_j)\ge 2t-z>t,
\tag{4}
\]
where each coordinate cap has area \(t/2\).  Consequently the physical
caps satisfy
\[
\boxed{\quad
|C_1+C_2+C_3|\ge q\,G(D).
\quad}
\tag{5}
\]
In particular, for the modulus \(\Delta_Q\) of accepted fact
`7bb6cb9b365924a5`,
\[
\boxed{\quad
\Delta_Q
\ge
\sqrt q\left(\sqrt{G(D)}-\sqrt{\frac{15}{7}}\right)
>
\sqrt q\left(\sqrt{G(D_*)}-\sqrt{\frac{15}{7}}\right)
>0.
\quad}
\tag{6}
\]
The strict uniform constant in (6) is exact; no numerical
infeasibility assertion is used.

Moreover, mixed-area additivity and planar Brunn--Minkowski give
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3\mathcal V(P,C_i)
=\mathcal V(P,C_1+C_2+C_3)
\ge\sqrt{pq\,G(D)}.
\tag{7}
\]
Therefore the boxed ledger inequality in accepted fact
`6e4bb19f9157027f` holds, and hence the fixed-ratio \(W=0\) realization is
excluded, whenever
\[
\boxed{\quad
\Xi\ge
\frac{13p}{4}+\frac{w_P}{3}-\frac{613q}{28}
-\frac12\sqrt{pq\,G(D)}.
\quad}
\tag{8}
\]
Equivalently, every realization still unresolved after (5)--(7) lies in
the sharply defined strict residual region
\[
0<D<D_*,
\qquad
\frac{Dp}{q}<1,
\tag{9}
\]
\[
0\le\frac{\Xi}{q}
<
\frac{13}{4}\frac pq+\frac{1}{3}\frac{w_P}{q}
-\frac{613}{28}
-\frac12\sqrt{\frac pq\,G(D)}.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus no further \(A_2\)-only lower bound asserting merely
\(\Delta_Q>0\) is the missing step.  The first remaining bridge is a
full common-plane lower bound on \(\Xi\) strong enough to reach (8), or a
stronger joint inequality coupling \(\Xi\) to the excess in (7).
